example.title: Solving for a Vector in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\-1 \\0 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix}- 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix},\quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.\]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ -x_1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -2x_2 \\ 3x_2 \\ -x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} 2x_3 \\ x_3 \\ -3x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1-2x_2+2x_3 \\ -x_1+3x_2+x_3 \\ -x_2-3x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-2x_2+2x_3 = 1 \\ -x_1+3x_2+x_3 = 0 \\ -x_2-3x_3 =1 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 + R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=R_3+ R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \end{array}\right]. \\ \end{align*}\]

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - 2x_2+2x_3 = 1 \\ x_2 +3x_3 = 1 \\ 0 = 2. \end{cases} \]

However, the final equation $0 = 2$ gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

example.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -5 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix} 3\\ 11 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -4 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a_1}+x_2 \mathbf{a_2} +x_3 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ -5 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_3 \begin{bmatrix}3\\ 11\\ -2\end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ 0 \\ 4x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -2x_2 \\ -5x_2 \\ -x_2 \end{bmatrix}+ \begin{bmatrix} 3x_3 \\ 11x_3 \\ -2x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -4 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1-2x_2+3x_3 \\ -5x_2+11x_3\\ 4x_1-x_2-2x_3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -4 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} x_1-2x_2+3x_3 =2 \\ -5x_2+11x_3= -4 \\ 4x_1-x_2-2x_3 = 15 \end{cases} \]

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \\ 4 & -1 & -2 & 15 \end{array} \right] \]

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

\[ \begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \\ 4 & -1 & -2 & 15 \end{array}\right] & R_3&:=R_3-4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 & -7 \end{array}\right]& R_3&\leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 & -7\\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \end{array}\right]& R_2&:=\dfrac17 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \end{array}\right]& R_3&:=R_3+5 R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right] . \\ \end{align*} \]

So, the system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 - 2x_2 + 3x_3 = 2 \\ x_2 -2x_3= 1 \\ x_3 = 1. \\ \end{cases} \]

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get \[ x_2 -2(1)= 1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_2 = 3.\] Finally, by substituting $x_2=3$ and $x_3=1$ into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1 - 2(3) + 3(1) = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=5. \]

So, the solution of the system is $x_1 = 5$, $x_2=3$, and $x_3 = 1,$ which means

\[ 5 \mathbf{a_1} + 3 \mathbf{a_2} + \mathbf{a_3} = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2+x_3 = 5 + 3 +1 = 9. \]

example.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.text:
Consider the vectors

\[ \mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix} -8 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -2 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}. \]

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
question.explanation:
If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1+x_2 \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{b}$, then we have

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} -8 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -2 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 3x_1 \\ 0 \\ -2x_1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -8x_2 \\ -x_2 \\ 4x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -2 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 3x_1-8x_2 \\ -x_2 \\ -2x_1+4x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -2 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} 3x_1-8x_2 = -1 \\ -x_2 = -2 \\ -2x_1+4x_2 = -2 \end{cases} \]

From the second equation we get $x_2=2$, which we substitute into the first equation to get \begin{align*} 3x_1-8x_2 &= -1 \\[3pt] 3x_1 - 8(2) &= -1 \\[3pt] 3x_1 &= 15 \\[3pt] x_1 &= 5. \end{align*}

Finally, we substitute $x_1=5$ and $x_2=2$ into the third equation to get

\begin{align*} -2x_1+4x_2 &= -2 \\[3pt] -2(5) + 4(2) &= -2 \\[3pt] -2 &= -2, \end{align*} which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is $x_1=5$ and $x_2=2,$ which means

\[ 5\mathbf{a_1}+2 \mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}. \]

Consequently,

\[ x_1+x_2=5+2=7. \]
